_meta.description: Reference data. Defines what each area of expertise means so that task authors, contributors and the routing engine share one vocabulary. Task.area and Contributor.expertise[].area both reference expertise_areas[].id.

levels.name: Foundational
levels.meaning: Understands the concepts and can do routine work under review. Not trusted to work unsupervised on ambiguous problems.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.meaning: Delivers standard work independently. Escalates unusual cases. Default minimum level for most tasks.

levels.name: Advanced
levels.meaning: Handles complex, ambiguous or cross-cutting work. Can review the work of Practitioners.

levels.name: Expert
levels.meaning: Recognised authority. Takes on high-risk, novel or externally-audited work and sets the standard others follow.

areas.name: Finance
areas.summary: Accounting, financial analysis, reconciliation and reporting for the business.
areas.description: Work that deals with money moving through the organisation and how it is measured and reported. This includes recording transactions correctly, reconciling records between systems, analysing variance between plan and actual, preparing management and statutory reports, and forecasting. A finance task usually has a numeric source of truth (ledger, invoices, bank statements) and a reviewer who will check totals. Accuracy, traceability of every number back to its source, and awareness of period cut-off rules matter more than speed. Finance work is frequently time-boxed to a close calendar, so lateness has a direct business cost.
in_scope: Budget vs. actual variance analysis and commentary
Account and invoice reconciliation (vendor, bank, intercompany)
Accruals, deferrals and month-end close support
Financial reporting packs and KPI calculation
Cash-flow and revenue forecasting
out_of_scope: Tax filing and legal advice (see legal_compliance)
Building data pipelines or dashboards (see data_analysis)

sub_skills.name: Variance analysis
sub_skills.description: Explain the difference between budget/forecast and actuals, separating timing differences from real drivers.

sub_skills.name: Reconciliation
sub_skills.description: Match two independent records, classify unmatched items and propose adjusting entries.

sub_skills.name: Month-end close
sub_skills.description: Accruals, prepayments, cut-off testing and close checklists.

sub_skills.name: Forecasting
sub_skills.description: Driver-based revenue, cost and cash forecasts with stated assumptions.

sub_skills.name: Financial reporting
sub_skills.description: Management packs, board summaries and statutory schedules.

level_rubric.1: Can code transactions and tick-and-tie simple reconciliations with a template.
level_rubric.2: Owns a routine reconciliation or variance report end-to-end and documents the unmatched items.
level_rubric.3: Runs a close workstream, designs the reconciliation approach, and challenges source data quality.
level_rubric.4: Signs off on externally-reviewed numbers, defines policy and handles audit questions.

example_tasks: Explain why Q3 travel spend is 18% over budget
Reconcile 3 months of vendor invoices against the AP ledger
Review the accrual schedule before month-end close

areas.name: Healthcare
areas.summary: Clinical operations, health data standards and patient-facing process knowledge.
areas.description: Work that requires understanding how care is delivered and how health information is recorded and protected. This covers clinical workflows (admission, intake, discharge, referral), health data standards and terminologies (ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC, HL7/FHIR), data quality in clinical systems, and the privacy rules that govern patient data. Healthcare tasks often involve sensitive information, so contributors must know what may and may not be copied into working files. A mistake can have patient-safety consequences, which is why healthcare tasks are often higher priority and need a higher minimum level than the same task would in another domain. Contributors do not need to be licensed clinicians, but they must be fluent in the vocabulary and the failure modes of clinical data.
in_scope: Auditing the quality and completeness of clinical or intake data
Mapping between clinical terminologies and code sets
Documenting and improving clinical or administrative workflows
Privacy and de-identification review of health datasets (technical, not legal opinion)
Interpreting clinical metrics (readmission, length of stay, wait times)
out_of_scope: Formal legal interpretation of health-privacy law (see legal_compliance)
General-purpose statistics unrelated to care delivery (see data_analysis)

sub_skills.name: Clinical data quality
sub_skills.description: Completeness, plausibility and consistency checks on intake and encounter records.

sub_skills.name: Terminology mapping
sub_skills.description: Cross-walk between ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC and local code sets, with documented ambiguity.

sub_skills.name: Clinical workflows
sub_skills.description: Admission, triage, referral and discharge process knowledge.

sub_skills.name: Health data privacy
sub_skills.description: PHI identification, minimum-necessary principle, de-identification methods.

sub_skills.name: Interoperability
sub_skills.description: HL7 v2, FHIR resources and the practical limits of data exchange between systems.

level_rubric.1: Knows common clinical terms and can follow a data-entry or review checklist.
level_rubric.2: Can audit a dataset against documented rules and flag records needing clinical review.
level_rubric.3: Maps terminologies with documented ambiguity, designs quality rules, and advises on PHI handling.
level_rubric.4: Clinical informatics authority: defines standards, resolves ambiguous mappings and advises on patient-safety impact.

typical_deliverables: Data quality audit report with record-level findings
example_tasks: Audit last month's patient intake forms for missing mandatory fields
Map the local diagnosis list to ICD-10-CM
Document the current discharge-planning workflow and its handoff gaps

areas.name: Data Analysis
areas.summary: Turning raw data into trustworthy answers: cleaning, analysis, metrics and visualisation.
areas.description: Work that starts with a question and a pile of data and ends with a defensible answer. It includes acquiring and cleaning data, exploratory analysis, defining metrics precisely, cohort and trend analysis, statistical reasoning, and communicating the result in tables or visuals that a decision-maker can act on. The area is domain-agnostic: it pairs with finance, healthcare or operations when the question is domain-specific, and stands alone when the challenge is the data itself. Good analysis states its assumptions, quantifies uncertainty, and shows how a number was derived so it can be reproduced. A task is rarely done when the chart is drawn; it is done when a reviewer can trace each claim to a query or calculation.
in_scope: Exploratory analysis and data profiling
Cohort, funnel, retention and trend analysis
Metric and KPI definition, including edge cases
Dashboard design and specification
Data cleaning, deduplication and validation rules
Basic statistical testing and sampling
out_of_scope: Data engineering infrastructure and pipeline operations
Domain interpretation that needs clinical or accounting expertise (pair with that area)

sub_skills.name: Data cleaning & profiling
sub_skills.description: Null, duplicate and outlier handling; profiling distributions before analysis.

sub_skills.name: Cohort & retention analysis
sub_skills.description: Group users or records by shared start event and track behaviour over time.

sub_skills.name: Metric definition
sub_skills.description: Unambiguous definitions with numerator, denominator, grain and exclusions.

sub_skills.name: Visualisation
sub_skills.description: Choose and build charts and dashboards that answer the question without misleading.

sub_skills.name: Statistical reasoning
sub_skills.description: Significance, confidence intervals, sampling bias and causal caution.

level_rubric.1: Can run provided queries, build simple charts and spot obvious data errors.
level_rubric.2: Frames a question, writes the queries and delivers a clear summary with caveats.
level_rubric.3: Handles messy multi-source data, designs metric frameworks and reviews others' analyses.
level_rubric.4: Sets analytical standards, handles causal-inference questions and advises on decisions with material impact.

example_tasks: Calculate 90-day retention by signup cohort and explain the Q2 drop
Define 'active customer' and document edge cases
Profile the customer table and list the top data-quality issues

areas.name: Operations
areas.summary: Running, measuring and improving the day-to-day processes that deliver the product or service.
areas.description: Work that keeps processes running and makes them better: logistics, fulfilment, service delivery, vendor and capacity management, incident response and continuous improvement. Operations contributors think in terms of flow, bottlenecks, handoffs, service levels and root causes. Typical tasks involve mapping how work actually happens (as opposed to how it is documented), finding where it stalls, proposing changes and defining how success will be measured. Incident-related tasks require calm, blameless investigation and a written record that prevents recurrence. This area is practical and cross-functional; deliverables are usually process maps, runbooks, root-cause analyses and improvement plans.
in_scope: Process mapping and bottleneck analysis
Incident investigation and post-incident reviews
Runbooks, SOPs and checklists
Capacity and workload planning
Vendor and service-level monitoring
Continuous-improvement proposals with measurable targets

sub_skills.name: Process mapping
sub_skills.description: Document the as-is process, handoffs and wait states from interviews and records.

sub_skills.name: Root-cause analysis
sub_skills.description: 5-whys, fishbone and timeline reconstruction without assigning blame.

sub_skills.name: Incident management
sub_skills.description: Triage, communication cadence, mitigation and post-incident review.

sub_skills.name: Capacity planning
sub_skills.description: Match workload forecasts to staffing and resource limits.

sub_skills.name: SLA & vendor management
sub_skills.description: Define, monitor and escalate on service-level commitments.

level_rubric.1: Can follow and update an existing runbook or checklist.
level_rubric.2: Maps a process end-to-end and identifies clear bottlenecks with supporting evidence.
level_rubric.3: Leads incident reviews, designs process changes and quantifies expected improvement.
level_rubric.4: Owns operational strategy, resolves cross-team conflicts and sets service-level policy.

example_tasks: Map the returns process from customer request to refund
Write the post-incident review for last week's shipping delay
Draft a runbook for the nightly batch failure

areas.name: Legal & Compliance
areas.summary: Interpreting rules, policies and contracts, and checking that the organisation meets them.
areas.description: Work that checks whether what the organisation does matches what it is obliged to do. This covers regulatory requirements (privacy, financial, industry-specific), internal policy, contract terms and audit readiness. Contributors read dense source material, map obligations to concrete controls, identify gaps and recommend remediation with a risk rating. Because the output can carry legal weight, the area distinguishes between compliance analysis (mapping obligations and spotting gaps) and formal legal opinion (which needs a qualified lawyer). Tasks in this area demand precision, explicit citations to the source clause, and a clear statement of what was and was not reviewed.
in_scope: Mapping a regulation or policy to internal controls
Gap assessment with risk ratings
Policy drafting and review (retention, access, acceptable use)
Contract clause review against a checklist
Audit evidence preparation

sub_skills.name: Privacy regulation
sub_skills.description: GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA obligations mapped to data handling practices.

sub_skills.name: Policy drafting & review
sub_skills.description: Retention, access-control and acceptable-use policies written to be enforceable.

sub_skills.name: Gap assessment
sub_skills.description: Compare current controls to requirements and rate each gap by risk.

sub_skills.name: Contract review
sub_skills.description: Checklist-based review of liability, data-processing and termination clauses.

sub_skills.name: Audit readiness
sub_skills.description: Collect and organise evidence so a control can be demonstrated.

level_rubric.1: Can locate and summarise relevant clauses with citations.
level_rubric.2: Completes a checklist-based review and flags obvious gaps.
level_rubric.3: Performs full gap assessments, drafts policy and prioritises remediation by risk.
level_rubric.4: Interprets ambiguous regulation, represents the organisation to auditors and sets compliance strategy.

example_tasks: Compare our data-retention policy with GDPR storage-limitation requirements
Review a vendor contract's data-processing clauses against the checklist
Assemble evidence for the quarterly access-review control

areas.name: Technical Writing
areas.summary: Turning complex knowledge into clear, accurate documentation for a specific audience.
areas.description: Work whose product is words and structure: onboarding guides, how-to articles, requirement documents, release notes, API or process documentation and training material. The craft is audience analysis (who will read this and what do they already know), information architecture, plain language, and verification (every step in a procedure must actually work when followed). Technical writers rely on subject-matter experts for content and are responsible for making it usable. Quality is judged by whether a new reader can complete the target task using only the document. Contributors in this area also review and edit others' drafts for consistency, tone and accuracy.
in_scope: Onboarding guides and how-to documentation
Requirement and specification documents
Runbooks and SOP write-ups (with Operations as subject-matter expert)
Release notes and change summaries
Editing and style-guide enforcement
out_of_scope: Original subject-matter analysis (pair with the relevant domain area)

sub_skills.name: Audience analysis
sub_skills.description: Identify reader goals, prior knowledge and the minimum they need to succeed.

sub_skills.name: Procedure writing
sub_skills.description: Numbered, testable steps with expected results and troubleshooting.

sub_skills.name: Information architecture
sub_skills.description: Structure, navigation and cross-linking for findability.

sub_skills.name: Editing & style
sub_skills.description: Consistency, terminology control and plain-language rewriting.

sub_skills.name: Requirements writing
sub_skills.description: Unambiguous, testable requirements and acceptance criteria.

level_rubric.1: Can proofread and apply a style guide to existing content.
level_rubric.2: Writes a clear how-to from SME notes and verifies the steps.
level_rubric.3: Designs a documentation set, interviews SMEs and tests docs with real users.
level_rubric.4: Defines documentation strategy and standards across teams.

example_tasks: Write the new-hire onboarding guide for the support team
Turn the incident review notes into a clean runbook
Rewrite the data dictionary in plain language
